args.subject_description: Same stocky orange tiger, broad middle-aged striped head, ivory muzzle, brown jacket, cream shirt, charcoal trousers, bare paws, single striped tail. Preserve face, proportions, costume, pixel density and screen-right south-east view in every frame.
args.initial_pose: Supplied crouched jump preparation, planted feet, low top-down south-east view.
args.action_description: One small vertical in-place jump with ANATOMICALLY DRAWN SQUASH AND STRETCH, then landing and settling. Intended as replacement key drawings for an existing jump, NOT a new attack. First bend knees and hips slightly deeper, pelvis drops and jacket bunches naturally while head keeps its normal shape. Next drive through toes with knees and ankles straightening: draw a slightly extended torso and legs at takeoff without scaling the face or whole sprite. One compact small airborne pose. Land on the same baseline with both feet planted; bend knees deeply and lower the pelvis to absorb the impact, jacket folds compress. Then rise gently into the supplied original neutral ending. Include a short readable compressed landing pose and a clear leg-straightening takeoff pose. Keep head proportions and tiger face unchanged, body mass believable, shoulders and pelvis connected. Small secondary tail settle allowed. No horizontal travel, no kick, no full turn, no uniform rubber-body scaling, no squash of the skull, no extra limbs, no VFX, no lines, no shadow, no environment. Transparent background, matching original pixel art.

args.subject_description: The exact supplied original orange tiger, broad striped head and ivory muzzle, brown jacket/cream shirt/dark trousers, same size and pixel-art style. Lock body/head/tail/feet in place; facing south-east screen right throughout.
args.initial_pose: Supplied original jab preparation with planted feet. Only the nearer punching forearm moves.
args.action_description: Only the VERY SHORT TRANSIT of one straight lead jab from the provided start to provided contact, no preparation or recovery. Keep the head, face, torso, opposite hand, legs, feet and tail matching the start image, fixed and coherent. The nearer fist travels a few pixels toward screen-right. In ONE intermediate drawing, exaggerate ONLY the connected striking forearm and fist into a short tapered ORANGE FLESH-COLOURED smear, continuous from brown cuff through wrist into the fist, aligned to the short horizontal jab. Resolve immediately into the supplied normal closed fist at contact. The anatomical smear is NOT a white effect, a detached trail, sword, beam, ring, duplicate fist or extra arm. Modest exaggeration, no huge reach, no motion of the rest of the character, no rotating head, no secondary punch, no jump, no speed lines or particles. Transparent original pixel-art background.

landingRequest.subject_description: Same original stocky orange tiger, striped head and cream muzzle, brown jacket, cream shirt, dark trousers, bare paws and one tail. Fixed south-east facing, same head size, same planted feet. Pixel art.
landingRequest.initial_pose: Supplied original landing crouch. BOTH FEET fixed to exactly their starting contact points.
landingRequest.action_description: A landing COMPRESSION AND REBOUND key-drawing study, no jump or upward takeoff. From the supplied crouch, draw the pelvis LOWER by approximately 5 logical pixels and bend the knees DEEPER, pushing thighs slightly outward and folding the brown jacket at the waist. The normal-sized head moves down with the shoulders about 4 pixels, keeping the face and skull UNCHANGED in size and expression. Make the compression visibly deeper than the supplied first frame: toes and soles remain on exactly the same baseline and locations, knees fold, belly and coat bunch, torso remains connected. One clear deepest crouch, briefly hold it, then knees unfold and the torso rises into the supplied final recovery pose. Do not simply copy the starting crouch. Do not uniformly scale the sprite or squash the skull. No standing up tall, no jump, no kick, no rotation, no motion lines, no VFX, no shadow. Transparent background with crisp original pixel clusters.

landingDrawing.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: ONE replacement landing-compression key drawing for this exact low-resolution pixel sprite. Edit the supplied tiger sprite, preserving the same individual tiger identity, striped orange-and-black broad head, ivory muzzle and cheeks, brown jacket over cream shirt, dark baggy trousers, bare tiger feet, single tail, same south-east view. The reference is already in a low landing crouch. Change ONLY the ANATOMICAL POSE to a visibly DEEPER shock-absorbing landing crouch: lower the pelvis another 5 logical pixels on the 96x96 reference grid, fold both knees outward and more sharply so the hips nearly sit between the heels, bring the shoulders and unchanged-size head downward about 4 pixels. Keep both bare feet at their EXACT same locations and same ground baseline. Keep the same head size, face angle and familiar face; NEVER flatten or shrink the skull. Bunch the brown jacket naturally at the waist and thighs. Hands remain near their original poses for balance. Preserve the reference's stocky body mass and clear connected joints. This must be a NEW DRAWN compressed joint pose, NOT the same pose, NOT a flattened or scaled copy. Render actual COARSE pixel-art clusters matching the 96x96 logical sprite (if output is enlarged, each logical pixel should be uniformly enlarged with sharp nearest-neighbor hard edges, no finer details). Preserve original palette, outline thickness, tiny eyes and simple shading. Composition matches original transparent square canvas: reference character occupies roughly x29..78 and y33..80 on the 96x96 logical grid; compressed result should keep foot baseline y80 but lower the top of the head toward y37, so character is about49 logical pixels wide and43 pixels tall. One character only, fully visible tail and feet. GENUINE transparent background. No ground, shadows, panels, text, labels, VFX, blur, trails, extra limbs, giant new fists, costume changes, smooth illustration or high-resolution detail.
